newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says on course for balanced budget.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says on course for balanced budget.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said Britain's public finances were steadily improving.
"The public finances are actually improving all the time," he told BBC Radio. "The level of borrowing is falling. We're heading for balance in the medium term."
Clarke said Britain had an enviable economic performance, with falling unemployment and low inflation combined with growth and competitiveness.
Clarke said the Conservative government had returned to its tax-cutting agenda after taking tough and necessary measures earlier in its present term of office.
He dismissed recent Labour party statements about its tax plans as evidence that the opposition favoured "a high-taxing, high-spending social democracy."
"We will nail them today with all the tax commitments they have already entered into," Clarke added, referring to the launch of a new Conservative election poster campaign.
